title: Random forest predictor RENOVO-NF1 classifies NF1 missense variant pathogenicity
summary: RENOVO-NF1 is a random forest predictor trained on 3,579 ClinVar variants whose classification stayed stable over time. It reached 96.5% accuracy on 57 variants initially labelled uncertain and later reclassified and 82% on a further 100 later-reclassified variants. The authors also report results on 15 de novo variants from a prospective clinical cohort; the abstract was read only, ClinVar labels carry circularity risk and the prospective set is small.
ai_technology: Random forest predictor (RENOVO-NF1) trained on stable ClinVar P/LP/B/LB variants to score NF1 missense variants

evidence.tested: Temporal test on variants reclassified after training (n=57, n=100) and a small cohort of 15 de novo variants; classified here as retrospective because the test labels are existing ClinVar data.
evidence.unknown: Accuracy on newly observed variants in routine diagnosis, label circularity with ClinVar, and the prospective result beyond n=15; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts pathogenic versus benign status of NF1 missense variants that are uncertain at detection.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations not retrieved. Full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
